title: Staged capacity failsafe and query-throttle tuning for hosted GPU pools
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Multiple recent hosted GPU exhaustion incidents manifested as fast queue growth followed by oscillatory throttling that harmed latency P95/P99 and caused customer errors. Root causes were a mix of large short-lived tenant bursts, KV-cache pollution on long sequences, and autoscaler hysteresis that primed capacity too slowly. Goal: build a staged failsafe that (1) detects oscillatory pool pressure early, (2) applies calibrated per-tenant soft-throttles and fast backfill policies, and (3) tunes admission and autoscaler hysteresis to avoid repeated thrash. Scope: hosted GPU pools only (not Dedicated/Private). This ticket covers detection signals, runtime admission scoring, emergency soft-shed, and a small set of telemetry and simulation experiments. Out of scope: heavy allocator/infra re-architecture and model-aware kernel changes (separate initiative).
updates: 2026-03-01 — Initial triage: incident review with on-call, SRE, runtime. Agreed to implement a 3-stage mitigation: (A) early oscillation detector, (B) tenant-weighted soft-throttle with progressive backfill, (C) autoscaler hysteresis tuning. Assigned owners and scoped MLOps sims.

2026-03-03 — Proof-of-concept: implemented a prototype oscillation detector that watches pool 'active_slots', 'queue_depth', and 'slot_hold_time' and computes an oscillation score (EMAs + zero-crossing of slope). Detector flagged two historical incidents in replay. Branch: github.com/redwood/runtime/pulls/3421 (POC).

2026-03-04 — Telemetry added: slot-level latency histograms and tenant ingress fingerprints to staging. Dashboard created: /dashboards/gpu-capacity/oscillation (internal). Early results: P99 reduction in simulation when soft-throttle is applied within 10s of detector firing.

2026-03-06 — Decision: soft-throttle must be progressive and tenant-weighted. We will reduce admission score by computed factor rather than hard-reject to preserve degraded but functional UX for high-priority tenants. Documented trade-off: slight increase in median latency in exchange for fewer errors and lower tail latency.

2026-03-08 — Simulation: ran tenant-mix replay (24-hour trace) with reservoir backlog limiter + soft-throttle. Results: queue tail depth reduced by 78%, mean token-per-second cost unchanged, error-rate down 63% during bursts. Simulation harness: github.com/redwood/sim/capacity/experiments/oscillation-2026-03.

2026-03-09 — Implemented runtime admission scoring change: exponential-moving admission score capped and decayed at tenant-level. Added fast backfill that allows short-lived preemptive capacity to serve in-flight KV-cached sequences. PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pulls/3457 (in review).

2026-03-10 — On-call runbook draft updated with 'oscillation mitigation' steps and emergency CLI commands to manually apply pool-level grace-rate. Routing/console UX owners notified to add a one-click 'soft-shed' control.

acceptance_criteria: Detector triggers on historical incidents in the simulation replay with >85% precision and <10% false positive rate.
Soft-throttle reduces P99 tail and error-rate by >=50% in replayed burst scenarios.
Autoscaler hysteresis changes do not increase mean time-to-scale beyond 2x current baseline in normal traffic patterns.
Console exposes soft-shed control and runbook entries; SRE validates with chaos test in staging.
All code changes merged, reviewed, and covered by unit + integration tests; feature gate toggles available for quick rollback.
runbook_summary: On-call quick steps: 1) Check detector score and pool slot histograms. 2) If detector >= threshold and queue growing, enable soft-shed for impacted tenants via CLI (grace factor 0.75) or console button. 3) Monitor P95/P99 and queue depth for 5 minutes; if no improvement, escalate to SRE and enable temporary pool-level backfill (adds short-lived preemptive slots). 4) If autoscaler lagging, trigger manual scale-up via internal autoscale API and open incident channel. 5) After mitigation, capture trace and hand off to Simulation for replay and root-cause tagging.
notes: Trade-offs: We prefer progressive soft-throttle to maintain availability for high-priority customers at cost of slightly increased median latency.
Future work: Explore tenant-aware KV-cache partitions and model-aware scheduling in a separate epic once immediate mitigations are validated.
Risk: Mistuned detector parameters could cause unnecessary throttles for noisy pools; will run A/B in staging before rollout.
